clinician.trajectory_summary: A 39-year-old man presented in May 2020 with a 6-month history of headache, paroxysmal blurred vision, tinnitus, numbness of the hands, cognitive slowing, and impaired memory. Initial neurological examination revealed cognitive slowing and impaired memory. MRI showed multiple round lesions in the corpus callosum, EEG showed paroxysmal short-range slow waves, and fundus fluorescein angiography showed dilated macular capillary and fluorescein leakage. Blood and CSF tests were normal. The patient was readmitted in April 2021 due to progression of symptoms, including paroxysmal visual field defect, headache, and hypoesthesia of the right hand, along with cognitive slowing and reduced tendon reflexes. Follow-up brain MRI remained unchanged. A skin biopsy performed in April 2021 revealed eosinophilic spherical inclusion bodies within sweat gland epithelial cell nuclei (E014). Concurrently, a molecular test showed a 101 GGC repeat in the 5′-untranslated region of the NOTCH2NLC gene (E013), confirming the diagnosis of NIID. The patient was prescribed oral analgesics and idebenone tablets. Follow-up 18 months after discharge revealed gradual relief of symptoms, with resolution of paroxysmal visual field defect and hypoesthesia of the hands, and only occasional headaches.
